subject: SDK compatibility and deprecation: mutual plan for v1 -> v2
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orchidtech.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@piper.io
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Heads up: OrchidTech SDK v1 deprecation impact & ask

Hi Naomi,

Quick note from our integration team — we're planning a major upgrade to OrchidTech's assistant product in Q4 and we depend on Redwood's SDK v1 semantics for session handling and KV persistence. Our engineers saw an earlier note about a v1->v2 deprecation window; can you share the upcoming timeline, compatibility guarantees, and any recommended migration shims?

Two asks:
- a formal deprecation date and grace period we can plan against
- a compatibility matrix that shows which v1 calls change behavior in v2 (auth, response streaming, and tool-calls are of particular concern)

We'd like to align roadmaps and propose a mutual action plan if Redwood can commit to coordinated release notes and a short canary period.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Integrations, OrchidTech

Subject: Re: Heads up: OrchidTech SDK v1 deprecation impact & ask

Samir — thanks for raising this. Good timing.

Short answers up front: we haven't locked a hard deprecation date yet, but we are targeting early Q1 2028 for v1 sunset with a 6-month grace period. That said, we want to work with top partners (OrchidTech included) to minimize friction.

Proposed next steps:
- internal sync with Redwood runtime team (Jonas) to validate breaking changes
- share a compat matrix draft (I'll attach a working spreadsheet)
- schedule a 45-min technical kickoff next week to draft a mutual action plan (MAP) and define a canary cohort

I've attached a draft compat matrix and a short SDK-shim proposal for internal discussion. Please confirm availability for a 45-min slot next Tue/Wed.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Partner Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: compat-matrix.xlsx]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Heads up: OrchidTech SDK v1 deprecation impact & ask

Hi all — quick technical note from runtime:

We did a line-item review of v1->v2 and the largest surface changes are:
- response streaming API signatures (chunk framing and event attributes)
- tool-calling contract tightening (structured tool outputs are now validated by default)
- session K/V semantics (namespacing changed for multi-tenant contexts)

Mitigations we propose:
1) a lightweight shim that exposes the v1 streaming endpoint but translates frames to v2 internally (performance hit ~2-4% in microbenchmarks).
2) a flagged compatibility mode for tool-calls that disables strict validation for a 90-day canary.
3) migration CLI that rewrites persisted session keys to the v2 namespacing scheme.

I'll attach a short proposal doc with implementation estimates. If OrchidTech can run a small canary (5% traffic) for 4 weeks, we can hit the early Q1 2028 sunset with low interruption.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
[attachment: redwood-sdk-shim-proposal.md]

Samir — adding a couple product/partnership notes:

1) Rollout policy: for strategic partners we can offer an extended grace period per account (additional 3 months) and a no-cost engineering sprint (up to 5 engineer-days) to help migration. We'll need a prioritized list of critical enterprise customers that would be impacted.
2) Notices & comms: we'll prepare joint release notes, and run partner-facing docs + migration guide in partner portal.
3) Compliance: if OrchidTech requires audit artifacts around session changes, we can provide a traceable migration report and the CLI rewrite logs.

Proposed dates:
- Technical kickoff: Wed 2027-07-07 09:00 PT
- Deliver compat matrix v1.1: Thu 2027-07-08
- Start canary window: Mon 2027-10-09

Please find the compat matrix attached; Samir, can you upload your migration plan to the Drive link so we can review pre-kickoff?

Thanks,

Redwood Inference

Best,
